text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish Queen Margrethe formally opened the 30 billion crown, 18-km tunnel/bridge fixed rail link over Denmark's Great Belt waterway linking Zealand island on which Copenhagen stands with the central island of Funen and the European mainland. The link reduces east-west train travel time by one hour, making train ferry services redundant after 114 years in operation. In June 1998, the biggest public works project in Danish history is due for completion when a road suspension bridge over the waterway opens.

--Danish wholesale group East Asiatic (EAC) intends to export pesticide to Burma in defiance of an international boycott of the military regime in Rangoon for its crackdown on democracy campaigners. The pesticide is to be sold in Burma through a Thailand-based associate company. The planned sale has caused dismay among two big Danish pension fund shareholders in EAC.
--Five Greater Copenhagen mayors are to find a total of 15 million crowns necessary for paying off the remaining debts incurred by the Copenhagen European Cultural Capital 1996 administration.

--There is a risk of new blockade action on German-Danish border crossing points in South Jutland by Danish export lorry drivers unhappy about employer proposals to only raise their tax-free foreign allowances by a minimal amount.

--Danish foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen expressed satisfaction with the Dutch European Union presidency's draft for a new EU treaty, notably its proposals for better environmental guarantees and new voting rules within the bloc.
